abstract.para: Whenever you create a disaster recovery system with &rear;, you must test it thoroughly on a test machine. The test machine must be able to serve as an identical replacement for the original machine if needed. We recommend testing the recovery system regularly to ensure everything works as expected.

listitem.para: You created a recovery system on the original machine.
The recovery system is available on a bootable recovery medium.
The test machine has identical hardware to the original machine.
The test storage is clean and as-new. This might mean never-used new storage or existing storage that is completely wiped. For more information, see

topic.para: Perform this procedure on the test machine:

step.para: Boot the test machine from the recovery medium.
Log in as &rootuser;. No password is needed.
Start the recovery installer, using the -D option to enable debugscript mode:
This command performs the following steps:

listitem.para: Restores the disk layout, including partitions, file systems and mount points.
Restores the system files and user files from the backup.

important.title: Using debugscript mode might log secrets
important.para: Using debugscript mode provides the most debugging information, including logging commands and arguments in the &rear; log file. However, secrets and sensitive information might also be logged. Make sure you remove or obscure this information before sharing the log file.

step.para: After the recovery process is finished, reboot the system:

Log in to the restored system with the original credentials. Check whether the system was successfully re-created and can serve as a replacement for the original machine in the production environment.

When the test is finished, wipe the test storage so that it's ready for the next test or a disaster. Wiping a storage device can take a long time, so we recommend having clean replacement storage ready before a disaster happens so that you can recover as quickly as possible.

topic.para: If the test fails, you might need to update the &rear; configuration and re-create the disaster recovery system.
